How much should you tip movers?

The standard tip for movers is $20–50 per mover for a local move, or 5–10% of the total move cost for larger jobs. For a 3-person crew on a standard local full-day move, budget $120–150 total ($40–50 per mover).

Unlike most tipped services, movers are typically tipped per person rather than as a percentage of the total, partly because move costs can be very high ($2,000–5,000+) and a percentage tip would be excessive, and partly because the physical effort is per-person rather than per-dollar.

Always tip after the move is complete and everything is in place. Assess the care taken with your belongings, how efficiently the crew worked, and whether they handled any difficult situations well before deciding the final amount. Hand each mover their tip in cash individually rather than giving a lump sum to the crew leader.

Factors that affect how much to tip movers

  • Move duration: Half-day moves (under 4 hours) warrant $20–30 per mover. Full-day moves (6+ hours) warrant $40–50 per mover. Moves that run over 8 hours deserve $50–100 per mover.
  • Difficulty: Stairs, narrow hallways, elevator waits, no parking close to the building, extreme heat or cold. All of these add physical and logistical burden. Tip toward the higher end for any difficult conditions.
  • Local vs long-distance: Local moves: $20–50/mover. Long-distance moves: $50–100/mover or 5–10% of total. Long-distance crews often work 10–12 hour days and drive between cities.
  • Care of belongings: If the crew handled fragile items with exceptional care, wrapped furniture properly, and placed everything exactly where you needed it, that deserves a stronger tip.
  • Disassembly/reassembly of furniture, packing and unpacking, specialty item handling (pianos, safes, art) all warrant tipping at the higher end of the range.

Movers tipping etiquette

Provide water, sports drinks, and snacks throughout the day. This is standard hospitality for a physically demanding job and is always appreciated. A pizza or lunch for a full-day crew is a thoughtful gesture that can be given alongside (not instead of) the cash tip.

For multi-day moves, tip at the end of each day rather than waiting until the final day. Each day's crew may be partially different, and daily tipping makes sure everyone who works gets paid.

If service was genuinely poor (items damaged, crew arrived very late, unprofessional behavior), a reduced tip of $10–15 per mover is fair rather than no tip at all. Document any damage separately through the moving company's claims process.

Frequently asked questions

How much should you tip movers?
Tip $20–50 per mover for a local move, or 5–10% of the total move cost for larger jobs. For a 3-person crew on a full-day local move, budget $120–150 total. Give each mover their tip in cash individually.
Should you tip movers per person or total?
Tip per person — hand each mover their own cash tip directly. Don't give a lump sum to the crew leader expecting it to be divided. $20–50 per mover for local, $50–100 per mover for long-distance or full-day moves.
How much do you tip movers for a local move?
Tip $20–30 per mover for a half-day local move (under 4 hours), and $40–50 per mover for a full-day move (6+ hours). For a 3-person crew on a full day, budget $120–150 total.
How much do you tip movers for a long-distance move?
Tip 5–10% of the total moving cost, or $50–100 per mover. A $3,000 long-distance move warrants $150–300 total ($50–100 per mover for a 3-person crew).
Is it rude not to tip movers?
Yes. Moving is physically grueling work — movers carry heavy furniture in all weather conditions all day. Not tipping a crew that performed well is considered rude. A reduced tip for poor service is better than nothing.
Should you tip more for a difficult move?
Yes. Tip toward the higher end ($50+ per mover) for moves with stairs, tight hallways, extreme weather, fragile or specialty items, or days that ran significantly longer than expected.
When should you tip movers — before or after?
Always tip after the move is complete. Wait until everything is unloaded and placed so you can assess the quality of work before deciding the final amount. Tipping before gives movers no incentive to take extra care.
Should you tip the moving truck driver separately?
If the driver is part of the crew, include them in the per-person tip. If the driver only drove and didn't load or unload, $20–30 is appropriate. Long-distance drivers who work alone warrant $50–100.
Do you tip movers from large companies?
If you hire labor through HireAHelper, TaskRabbit, or similar services, tip $20–50 per person as normal. PODS or U-Haul equipment drop-off drivers don't typically receive tips, but $10–20 is a nice gesture for great service.
Besides tipping, how else can you show appreciation to movers?
Provide water, sports drinks, and snacks throughout the day. A pizza or lunch for a full-day crew is a thoughtful gesture. These extras should supplement, not replace, a cash tip.
